content.content: Understand how to load a self-tailing winch and safely use line clutches.

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Winches & Clutches'?

sideB.content: Understand how to load a self-tailing winch and safely use line clutches.

content.content: Primary mast security. Inspect chainplates, turnbuckles, pins and cotters for cracks, corrosion, and proper seizing.

Replace bent/missing cotter pins; tape sharp ends
Check for crevice corrosion at deck penetrations
Turnbuckle collars/locknuts secure; threads clean

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Chainplates, Turnbuckles & Cotter Pins'?

sideB.content: Primary mast security. Inspect chainplates, turnbuckles, pins and cotters for cracks, corrosion, and proper seizing.

content.content: Correct tension maintains mast column. Sight up the mast for straightness and tune leeward/ windward tensions evenly.

Use a rig tension gauge or builder’s guide
After sailing, adjust until leeward shrouds just slack
Re-check after new wire/seasonal changes

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Shrouds & Stays Tension (LOA Check)'?

sideB.content: Correct tension maintains mast column. Sight up the mast for straightness and tune leeward/ windward tensions evenly.

content.content: Structural interfaces take high loads. Look for cracking, movement, or leaks at step and partners.

Verify partners wedges/chocks snug and sealed
Check step fasteners, mast boot or sealant
Inspect compression post/base for crushing

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Mast Step, Partners & Compression Post'?

sideB.content: Structural interfaces take high loads. Look for cracking, movement, or leaks at step and partners.

content.content: Reliable hoists depend on sound halyards, sheaves, and terminations.

Inspect cover wear at clutches and sheaves
Mouse/tag ends before unreeving
Swap ends seasonally to spread wear

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Halyards (Main/Headsail/Spinnaker)'?

sideB.content: Reliable hoists depend on sound halyards, sheaves, and terminations.

content.content: Primary control lines for trim; keep fair, labeled, and managed.

Check chafe at clew rings and blocks
Whip or heat-seal bitter ends; add labels
Flake/stow tails clear of winches and pedals

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Sheets (Main/Genoa/Jib) & Tails'?

sideB.content: Primary control lines for trim; keep fair, labeled, and managed.

content.content: Fast, clean reefing protects rig and crew when wind builds.

Lead reef lines cleanly; mark tack/clew positions
Cunningham/halyard ease coordinated with reef
Keep reefing hooks/ram’s horn accessible

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Reefing System (Slab/In‑Boom)'?

sideB.content: Fast, clean reefing protects rig and crew when wind builds.

content.content: Controls leech tension and twist; prevents boom lift offwind.

Inspect tackle, cascades, or gas strut integrity
Attachment points sound at boom and mast base
Ease before heavy gybes; re-tension after

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Boom Vang (Rigid/Line)'?

sideB.content: Controls leech tension and twist; prevents boom lift offwind.

content.content: Traveler controls angle of attack; maintain bearings and controls.

Traveler control lines free; stops intact
Car bearings smooth under load
Center and lock before dock/anchor

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Mainsheet Traveler & Car (Rigging)'?

sideB.content: Traveler controls angle of attack; maintain bearings and controls.

content.content: Proper lead angle shapes the headsail and protects the sail.

Pins fully seated; cars locked before tacks
Adjust lead to split luff telltales evenly
Lube track fasteners lightly to deter seizure

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Genoa/Jib Cars & Tracks (Rigging)'?

sideB.content: Proper lead angle shapes the headsail and protects the sail.

content.content: Smooth furling reduces deck work and risk in breeze.

Fair lead to drum; no overrides on the furling line
Halyard restrainer to prevent halyard wrap
Toggle/pins/cotters secured; spins freely

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Headsail Furler & Extrusions'?

sideB.content: Smooth furling reduces deck work and risk in breeze.

content.content: Pre-rig preventers to control the boom on deep angles.

Rig outboard to bow/stanchion base padeyes
Quick-release at cockpit; never to lifelines
Ease before turning up; re-set on new jibe

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Preventer System (Gybe Control)'?

sideB.content: Pre-rig preventers to control the boom on deep angles.

content.content: Fore‑and‑aft rig tension tool; also supports masthead.

Hydraulic/mechanical adjuster operates smoothly
Inspect split/rod terminals and toggles
Ease in light air; tension for upwind/flat main

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Backstay / Adjuster (or Running Backs)'?

sideB.content: Fore‑and‑aft rig tension tool; also supports masthead.

content.content: Controls draft along the foot of the main.

Check clew slug/shackle and boom sheaves
Lead minimizes friction; mark reference settings
Ease for power offwind; tension for pointing

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Outhaul & Foot Tension'?

sideB.content: Controls draft along the foot of the main.

content.content: Fine-tunes luff tension for shape and depower.

Hook or ring secured near the tack
Lead clear of spreaders/instruments
Use as first depower with vang/traveler

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Cunningham / Downhaul'?

sideB.content: Fine-tunes luff tension for shape and depower.

content.content: Simplify hoists and drops; manage chafe where lines cross the sail.

Set spread to avoid batten snag
Ease topping lift under sail; tension at anchor
Chafe patches where lines contact sail

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Lazy Jacks / Topping Lift'?

sideB.content: Simplify hoists and drops; manage chafe where lines cross the sail.
